title: Prompt-cache TTL per agent role
brief: Parked: workers on 5m cache TTL, waiting sessions on 1h — operator deciding
body:
Claude Code gives a subscription's main session a 1-hour prompt-cache TTL (cache write 2× base input) and subagents/forks 5 minutes (1.25×); every lyx agent is a main session in tmux, so all of them write at the 1-hour price (see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching.md).

Measured on the `landing` run's transcripts: Discussion, Plan, Bouncer and Burler never paused more than 90 s between turns, so 5 minutes keeps them warm; ly-drive paused up to 508 s (three gaps over 5 minutes), so it needs 1 hour. Webster Master waits on forks via Monitor and is not yet measured.

Likely shape: shuttle sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=5m|1h` (Claude Code v2.1.242+) per role when it spawns a session, configurable per role. loomyard was developed with the 5-minute limit in mind, so 5 minutes matches its design assumption.

title: Burler: round-N focus directive conflicts with the read-prior-rounds-last rule
brief: Focus directive needs prior-round files the round prompt says to read only after the review
body:
Friction from run `operator-surface`, Burler Webster-Review round 2 (stencils from `d619100af`).
The round-2 focus directive asked the reviewer to check the round-1 F4 site list and the round-1 fix commits, which requires reading `round-1-review.md` and `round-1-fixer-report.md`.
The round prompt's instruction 2 says prior-round files are read only after the review is saved, so the focus file handed over in instruction 1 cannot be followed without breaking it; the reviewer read them early and said so.
Fix direction: the focus directive restates the sites it depends on, or the prior-round rule exempts what a focus directive names.

title: loom start races the ly-drive self-removal and ends with no driver
brief: First loom start after a hand-back keeps a strand that is about to be removed
body:
After a hand-back, the ly-drive session removes its own strand with a detached `lyx reed remove --name loom-driver --detach` that waits for the session's pid to exit (end-of-session command from `083e992cf`).
A `lyx loom start` issued in that window sees the loom-driver strand still live, keeps it instead of spawning a driver, and the detached remover then deletes it: the run is left with no driver and nothing happens (hit on `batten-hub-ready` and `focus-marker-warn`, 2026-09-30; a second `loom start` works).
Fix direction: `loom start` treats a driver strand with a pending self-removal (or whose claude has exited) as gone and spawns a fresh one, or the remover skips a strand that was re-adopted since it was scheduled.

title: Landing verify gate skips a merge interrupted before its marker write
brief: A crash between the merge-in commit and the pending-verify marker write leaves the next resume seeing up-to-date with no marker, so verify is skipped.
body:
Found reviewing PR #308 (`publish-verify-after-merge`).
Fabric reports a finished-but-interrupted merge as already up to date, so the gate cannot tell a verified tree from an unverified one.
Robust fix: record the task HEAD that last passed verify, and verify whenever HEAD differs from it.

title: fabric remove leaves the pair tmux session alive
brief: After `lyx fabric remove` the pair tmux session (driver claude, status strand, bash) keeps running in the deleted directory; its late writes recreate the worktree dir as a stray folder.
body:
Seen 2026-09-30 for quarry-cli-answers and status-strand-by-driver: after landing and `fabric remove --remote`, their reed sessions were still alive hours later.
A driver that wrote its stop report after the removal recreated `<hub>/<slug>/.lyx/...` and `<hub>/<slug>/_lyx/shed/<slug>/drive-reports/<report>.md`: a stray directory, and a drive report that never reached the archive.
The hub killed the sessions and deleted the dirs by hand.

Fix: remove (and batten teardown) ends the pair reed session (reed down) before deleting the worktrees, and waits for or refuses on a live driver; a stop report written after done should land before the archive tag.

title: batten run right after loom start exits on the child's stale blocked state
brief: loom start returns ok before the child status leaves blocked; an immediate lyx batten run reads blocked and exits again
body:
Seen 2026-09-30 on batten-records-leak-into-pairs: after a hub fix, `lyx loom start --no-attach` (ok) followed at once by `lyx batten run` ended with Run-Shed "inner shed run reached state blocked" because status.json still said blocked for a few seconds.
Fix direction: loom start writes state running (or a resume marker) before returning, or batten treats a blocked child whose driver was just relaunched as running.

title: Process naming and parentage: every process lyx spawns has a name and knows its parent
brief: Lift strand naming out of the creel design into its own module, and record a parent per worktree so every question from a run goes to the session that spawned it
body:
Operator 2026-09-30/10-01: wants a proper naming system so processes are easy to find, out of creel and general; and every worktree thread must know its parent: if the hub spawns a worktree, the hub is the parent of every process in it, and all questions go to the hub.
Today children show up as auto names like `refusal-audit-c9`; nothing of the naming part of manifest/designs/reed-mailbox.md is built.
Naming: `<role>@<slug>` grammar owned by one package, fixed role vocabulary (orch, driver, worker, reviewer, operator); the strand name is a birth attribute in reed state, mirrored to the pane title (allow-set-title off), the Claude session name (`claude --name`) and `LYX_STRAND_NAME`; the reed watchdog restores drifted mirrors (Claude resets the session name after compact); `lyx reed list` as the directory.
Parentage: the spawner records `parent` (its own address) in the run seed at create time (batten run / loom start); every strand reed starts in that worktree gets `LYX_PARENT`; stencils tell agents that questions and notices go to `$LYX_PARENT`; no parent recorded means the operator (awaiting state).
Delivery v1: Claude Code peer messaging (SendMessage to the parent's session name, used successfully 2026-09-30), which needs session name == strand name; creel replaces it later without changing the addresses.
The hub itself must carry a stable name (orch@<hub>), set by lyx orch or by the hub at session start.
Prerequisite for orch-discussion-review's live question mode.

title: lyx orch: ready to host the real hub orchestrator
brief: orch is deployed but untested live and lacks what the hub needs: bypass permissions, the Agent tool, adoption of a running session, a soft threshold
body:
Found 2026-09-30:
- orch launches as an interactive shuttle run (internal/orchcli/start.go:61), so no --dangerously-skip-permissions; the hub runs in bypass mode. Want a permission-mode option, bypass as the orch default.
- shuttle denies the Agent tool in every run (claude_deny_agent_tool), so orch cannot spawn review or fix agents; ForkSubagents is false.
- no way to adopt a running session (`--adopt <session-id>` via claude --resume, watcher bound to the existing transcript).
- soft threshold: hand off at a natural break from about 300k, 400k hard cap.
- risk: SessionIdle may read Claude's greyed prompt suggestion as not idle, so no cycle ever runs; verify live.

title: Orchestrator reviews the discussion: loom port of mill-start --orch
brief: Hub runs never involve the orchestrator in Discussion; port millhouse's mill-start --orch + orch-review/orch-wait so the hub writes Discussion-Review round 1
body:
Operator 2026-09-30: a weakness that the orchestrator is not involved during discussion; millhouse's `mill-start --orch` with the `orch-review`/`orch-wait` skills works very well.
Mill shape: the worker pauses before discussion-review round 1, messages its parent session (`--parent <name>`) that discussion.md is ready, and waits for `orch-review.md`; the orchestrator forks a reviewer that writes it in the review-output format (BLOCKING/NIT, class design/scope/decision/consistency); the worker fixes and continues; convergence needs two consecutive APPROVEs, so round 1 alone never converges; round 2+ uses the normal reviewer.
Loom shape to decide: a seed flag (batten sets it for hub runs) that makes Discussion-Review round 1 an `awaiting` stop naming the discussion file; the hub writes its review and records it with a verb (reuse the approve/reject record idiom), and `lyx loom start` resumes; the notification can be the awaiting state (hub watch) plus a message to the parent once process-naming exists.
Open: the same for Plan-Review round 1.

title: Convergence: measure hub and driver interventions, fix at the source, hardening freezes
brief: Plan for lyx to converge rather than accumulate bugs: per-run intervention log, real-wiring tests, feature freezes
body:
Operator 2026-09-30: take a step back and plan for convergence, not keep accepting more bugs.
Observed today: nearly every hub intervention was in same-day new code (#319: approve nil dep, reject reading its file argument as run-id), and both passed tests built on fake deps.
Ingredients: (1) log every hub intervention and ly-drive repair per run with a class and cause, so interventions per run and new-vs-repeat failure classes are visible; (2) every fix at the source with a test that drives the real CLI wiring, not only fakes; (3) freeze periods with no new verbs or recipe rows, hardening only, until the intervention rate flattens.
Goal: the outside LLM steps in rarely, and for the task rather than for lyx.

title: Bolt as the roadmap: three numbered tiers in one store, rendered like roadmap.md
brief: Bolt's README is unreadable; give bolt the roadmap's three tiers as a tier number in one entry store and render it in the roadmap's one-line-per-item style
body:
Operator 2026-10-01: manifest/roadmap.md is very readable, bolt's README is not readable at all; bolt should follow the roadmap's principle, and everything in it matters to the orchestrator (the future direction shapes how Planned work is reviewed).
Tiers: 1 = concretized and claimable (rendered Planned); 2 = planned to be done next but not concretized, not claimable until promoted (Next Up); 3 = loose ideas the operator has thought about, as in roadmap.md today (Someday).
Storage: one store, not tasks.json + notes.json (and not three files): every entry carries a numeric `tier`; the data holds only the number and the renderer alone owns the section names. Claimable means tier 1; promotion is a lower tier number (3 -> 2 -> 1, skip allowed as in the roadmap); new ideas default to tier 3. The task and notes verb groups collapse onto it; migrate the two existing files.
Render README like roadmap.md: one section per tier, in tier order, each with a one-line meaning, one `1.` item per entry with **title**, slug, one or two what/why sentences and the design link, no per-entry headings and no numeric ids; optionally live state/producer/PR on running tier-1 entries.
Folds in board-prune-done (one verb removing every done entry, its design doc and dangling depends_on).
After the manifest triage, roadmap.md's Someday moves into bolt and bolt becomes the only roadmap.
Content job, not code: rewrite entry briefs as what/why during the review.

brief: lyx agents get the constraints directive only when _lyx/PATTERN.md exists, and loomyard has none, so every run so far ran without it; CONSTRAINTS.md is the millhouse-style setup that PATTERN replaces
body:
Operator 2026-10-01: CONSTRAINTS.md is millhouse's setup; loomyard's variant is PATTERN, not yet initialized.
Verified: no _lyx/PATTERN.md in loomyard-weft, and there is no init verb. internal/pattern injects a role directive (implementer, review-fix, orchestrator) pointing at _lyx/PATTERN.md into webster fork/Master, burler and loom plan prompts only when the file exists, so today's runs got no PATTERN directive (they only saw CONSTRAINTS.md through CLAUDE.md and stencil mentions).
Work: move CONSTRAINTS.md's invariants into _lyx/PATTERN.md (weft, invisible to the code repo; optionally split under _lyx/pattern/); repoint everything that names CONSTRAINTS.md: CLAUDE.md, stencils (loom discussion/plan/rework, webster master and prefix-recovery), the ly-drive skill, contracts/specs, burlercli/run.go, loomshed and treadleengine docs, and contracts/stencils/citation_enforcement_test.go; decide whether a `lyx pattern init` verb is wanted for other repos.
